Gouache and ink painting on cream notebook paper, loose student sketchbook style, visible brushwork, pooled washes, a little pencil under-drawing. A flat concrete rooftop at night seen from the back of an open-air film screening. A blank dark rectangular projection screen stands on two poles in the upper middle of the picture. Behind a low parapet, a dense harbour city skyline of tall towers with small warm lit windows. An olive-green tarpaulin sags across the top of the picture in scallops, tied with ropes to poles at left and right; rain falls beyond it. A cylindrical water tank on a steel stand at far left, a small stair-head door at far right. The lower half is empty wet concrete in deep indigo, evenly dark. The painting stops short of the paper edge with a ragged unpainted cream margin. Deep indigo, slate and olive, with tiny warm yellow window lights. No people, no figures, no faces, no hands. No text, letters, numbers or signage anywhere. Not a photograph, not a 3D render.

Landscape 3:2. Highest fidelity to this exact art direction; no extra elements. This is a style exploration, not a book mockup.

Fictional actors, not resembling any real person. No text, no subtitles, no watermark.
